subject: QuantBank: unexpected queueing and 5xx fallout on reserved pool — exec escalation
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@quantbank.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected queueing and 5xx errors on reserved pool (QuantBank / Redwood)

Sergio —

We started seeing a spike in latency and a corresponding uptick in 500-level errors across our reserved endpoint (reserve id QB-RSV1) at ~08:55 PDT. Throughput dropped by ~40% and a subset of requests are timing out. This coincided with a burst in inference requests from a nightly job, but the error rate is affecting live traffic as well.

Attached: request-trace.zip (small traces + example request ids).

Impact: pages for our fraud-check pipeline are delayed >4s and 0.8% of calls are returning 5xx. We are seeing queueing on the dedicated GPU pool and several requests stuck in redis for long tail. This is causing customer-facing failures.

Can Redwood confirm whether there was any autoscale or scheduling change on the dedicated pools this morning and advise immediate mitigation steps? We need an exec-level point of contact — this is affecting our production SLA.

—Oliver
VP, Engineering
QuantBank

Sergio

Subject: Escalation: Dedicated pool saturation for QB-RSV1 — immediate ops play

Team —
We need an executable mitigation now. Executive summary: dedicated GPU pool for QuantBank (QB-RSV1) is saturated; queueing has produced 5xx errors and service-level regressions. This requires burst authorization + a short-term routing fallback to avoid SLA exposure.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Rishi: push burst capacity (add 4x burst nodes to QB-RSV1) and confirm scheduling changes (ETA 20 min). Attach route_logs_20261009.csv.
- Vivek: prioritize KV cache eviction and aggressive prefix offload for the fraud-check route (ETA 15 min).
- Naomi: coordinate customer-facing messaging and confirm acceptance of hosted fallbacks for non-PII traffic (ETA 10 min).
- Sergio: notify execs and request approval for one-time credit if SLA is violated.

I’ve attached a short SLA impact summary for the execs (SLA-impact-summary.pdf) and opened an incident: https://incident.redwood.local/INC-20261009-1492

Do not schedule any batch jobs against that pool until we’re stable. Keep replies tight — I’ll coordinate the bridge.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver@quantbank.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Dedicated pool saturation for QB-RSV1 — immediate ops play

Status update and resolution summary:
- At 10:08 PDT we executed burst add (+4 nodes) on QB-RSV1, and at 10:14 PDT we enabled aggressive KV eviction for the fraud-check route.
- Observed results: median latency dropped from 1.8s to 0.6s for the route; 5xx errors reduced from 0.8% to 0.02% across the last 30 minutes. Queue depth returned to normal.
- Root cause (preliminary): a latent job misconfiguration pushed a high rate of long-seq inference requests (sequence length > 3k) into the reserved pool during the nightly window; our scheduler did not preempt them quickly enough.

Next steps:
1) Rishi to ship a scheduler patch that adds an early-preempt rule for long-seq background jobs to avoid headroom erosion (PR filed: https://git.internal/redwood/scheduler/pulls/724).
2) We will run a backfill of route-level throttles to avoid cross-tenant spillovers; ETA for full rollout 72 hours.
3) Customer remediation: Sergio/Naomi — offer a one-time credit and a postmortem with action items.

Oliver — we’ve attached the cleaned route logs (route_logs_20261009.csv) and a short artifact showing 5xx timelines. If you’re good, we’ll leave the burst nodes in place for 2 hours and then scale down.

Thanks everyone; keeping the bridge open for one more hour for handoff.

—Vivek
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
